teams.product_capability: A pre-registered, deterministic falsification harness plus a single named geometry decision for the query map: an audited statement of whether the shipped map's proximity, clusters, labels, outliers and relation edges actually satisfy the Master Prompt / QUERY_MAP_MVP §7 minimum semantics and §11's cluster-stability metric on the exact bundles a jurist will be shown, and — if they do not — a bounded, budget-compliant alternative or an accepted negative result.
teams.question: On the committed, accepted query_result_bundles, does the current query-conditioned geometry (TF-IDF -> TruncatedSVD(n_components=2) -> KMeans, product/query/qmap.py at lab/product 0f0e9f7) make screen proximity mean query-conditioned similarity, clusters mean coherent groups, labels mean why the group exists, outliers mean weakly connected decisions, and citation/relation edges mean anything at all — under thresholds and input hashes frozen BEFORE any number is computed?
teams.hypothesis: Probably yes for clustering coherence (KMeans runs on the full TF-IDF space, not the 2-D projection) and probably NO for the projection and for labels and relations. TruncatedSVD to 2 components of a sparse TF-IDF matrix of 100-300 decisions is a lossy, unvalidated embedding of neighbourhood structure, so 2-D distance is unlikely to track cosine similarity; the stopword filter in qmap.py clearly misses German/French grammatical fragments, so top-term labels are likely junk rather than legal concepts; the outlier rule (top 10% by distance to own centroid) may just re-flag the retrieval tail; and _finalise's shared-citation relation extractor may yield the empty set on every realistic query. If a criterion FAILS, at most three named alternatives (metric MDS on cosine, UMAP if importable, query-anchored 2-D) are evaluated under the same frozen rule inside the §9A local-geometry budget (<2 s for 100-300 decisions); if none passes within budget, the negative result is recorded and the current geometry is kept.
teams.why_now: Concrete defects read directly out of accepted artifacts, not a general research idea. (a) results/product/gate_rehearsal/CYCLE_38754777366_live_bundle.json (227 live OpenCaseLaw decisions) has ONE cluster of 186/227 = 81.9% and its label is 'abs, in, stpo, iv, sein'; results/product/clickable_slice/bundle_live_enriched_CYCLE_38740365477.json (287 decisions) has one cluster of 195/287 = 68.0% labelled 'stgb, in, haftung, dass, wegen'. A cluster holding 82% of the result set is not a branch, and MP §7 says a cluster is a locally coherent group whose label explains why it exists. (b) Labels across the three committed bundles are dominated by function-word and citation fragments the stopword list missed: 'in', 'abs', 'ch', 'cp', 'dass', 'wegen', 'novembre', 'fors', 'zugefügt', 'iii', 'or'. (c) All three committed bundles have relations == [] (0 edges), so MP §7's 'citation/relation edges available on selection' and §9's 'relation edges on selection' are undemonstrated in the very artifacts the owner session will render. (d) In all three bundles the x coordinate range is [0.0, max] with min exactly 0.0 — half the canvas unused, an artifact of _canonicalise_axes plus the np.clip(coords,-1,1) in project_into_model that also means projected points pile on the boundary. (e) The integrated evaluator's active_metrics (accepted state evaluation.json, direction 45) contain geometry PRESERVATION and DETERMINISM but never geometry SEMANTICS, so nothing in the accepted chain has ever checked §11's cluster stability. (f) The comparative human gate is imminent and one-shot: MP gate questions 1 and 2 ask whether the map exposed a branch less visible in the list and whether it made structure easier to understand. A map whose proximity does not mean similarity cannot answer those questions for any reason an agent could not fix first. (g) REUSE-FIRST: qmap.py, pipeline.py and the committed bundles already exist; this is a measurement and a decision, not a rebuild.

teams.acceptance_test: (1) FREEZE FIRST: commit results/frontier/frontier-map-semantics/RULES.json before computing anything — it must contain the input bundle file names and their sha256, the exact metric definitions, and every PASS/FAIL threshold, with a UTC timestamp earlier than any measured artifact. Editing a threshold after seeing a number invalidates the run and must be declared. (2) A runnable offline harness (python -m frontier_map_semantics.cli --bundle <path> --out <dir>, plus --frozen-rules) that recomputes the map from the bundle's own texts and emits, per bundle: (a) projection fidelity — Spearman between 2-D Euclidean distance and TF-IDF cosine distance, and kNN@10 overlap between 2-D neighbours and cosine neighbours; (b) rank fidelity — Spearman between distance-to-query-vector and retrieval rank; (c) cluster structure — largest-cluster share, and mean intra-cluster vs inter-cluster cosine separation ratio; (d) label informativeness — distinct-label count, mean pairwise Jaccard between label term sets, and the fraction of label terms that are NOT stopwords and NOT BGE/ATF citation fragments; (e) outlier validity — mean shared-citation degree and mean retrieval rank of flagged vs unflagged rows, plus whether the flagged set is merely the rank tail; (f) relations — edge count, and whether the extractor is incapable of producing edges (measured by re-running it on the rows' own citation fields) rather than merely finding none. (3) Every criterion is reported PASS/FAIL against the frozen thresholds, with no metric dropped, silently reweighted or omitted. (4) NON-VACUITY: the same harness must be shown to FAIL on a deliberately corrupted geometry (cluster ids and labels permuted across clusters), so a PASS is demonstrably informative; record that run. (5) At least three bundles, of which at least two must be live-derived and one must be the 227-decision gate-rehearsal bundle; identical inputs must produce a byte-identical report. (6) IF AND ONLY IF a geometry criterion FAILS: evaluate at most three named alternatives (metric MDS on cosine, UMAP if importable, query-anchored 2-D) under the identical frozen rule and the §9A budget of < 2 s local geometry for 100-300 decisions, and report the best plus each one's measured wall time. If none passes within budget, record the NEGATIVE result and recommend keeping the current geometry. (7) A short report (reports/frontier/frontier-map-semantics/) naming exactly ONE geometry decision for product in one sentence, with the numbers behind it, plus the integration contract saying explicitly that product owns any code change. teams.product_capability: An audited, pre-registered measurement of whether the product genuinely EXECUTES the Master Prompt's independent adversarial retrieval pass and whether contrary/limiting authority is actually made discoverable by the map rather than only re-labelled at the top of the conventional ranked list — plus, if the pass is retrieval-blind, one bounded, named diagnosis of why, handed to product as a decision input.
teams.question: Across the frozen reality-check legs and the committed accepted bundles, does the adversarial counter-authority pass contribute decisions the initial broad retrieval did NOT retrieve, and does it place contrary/limiting authority where the map makes it visible (its own cluster, an outlier, or a toggled state) rather than inside the same mega-cluster as the consensus — the 227-bundle counter rows sit at ranks 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 13 and the 287-bundle counter rows span ranks 1-27 (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 22, 27) — that the conventional ranked list already shows first?
teams.hypothesis: No — and that is the finding that matters. The adversarial pass is currently classification over the initial candidate pool, not an independent retrieval pass: every counter-labelled row in the accepted live bundles carries channel search / search.language_filter / citation.outgoing / citation.incoming, i.e. provenance identical to the initial broad search, and every one of them sits at the very top of the conventional rank order. If that generalises, the product can claim it 'searches for contrary authority' while never retrieving anything the broad pass missed, and the map adds nothing to counter-authority discovery that answer + ranked list did not already show first — which is exactly the product hypothesis the human gate is about to test. A second, testable suspicion: the status gate is too conservative, collapsing genuine limiting/contrary findings into unclassified (221/227 unclassified on the corporate-liability bundle).
teams.why_now: Concrete measurements read from accepted artifacts on lab/product 0f0e9f7, not a general idea. (a) results/product/gate_rehearsal/CYCLE_38754777366_live_bundle.json (227 decisions, live, query 'Responsabilite penale de l'entreprise selon l'art. 102 CP'): counter_status distribution is 221 none / 3 cited / 2 candidate-limiting / 1 candidate-contrary, and provenance.generative_audit.status_summary reports supporting 3, limiting 2, contrary_or_exception 1, unclassified 221 — a 0.9% adversarial yield. (b) results/product/clickable_slice/bundle_live_enriched_CYCLE_38740365477.json (287 decisions): 273 none / 10 cited / 4 candidate-limiting / 0 candidate-contrary. (c) Rank placement: in the 227-bundle the counter rows are ranks 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 13; in the 287-bundle they are ranks 1-27. A conventional ranked list shows exactly those first, so MP gate question 1 ('the map exposed a relevant branch/case/exception that was LESS VISIBLE in the ranked list') currently has no positive instance, and gate question 3 ('the map increased confidence that contrary authority had not simply been hidden') has nothing hidden to reveal. (d) Placement: 5 of 6 counter rows in the 227-bundle and 13 of 14 in the 287-bundle sit inside the same mega-cluster as the consensus, and NONE is flagged is_outlier — so counter-authorities are not positionally discoverable either. (e) Channel provenance: retrieval.candidate_channels for the 227-bundle is {search 125, search.language_filter 98, leading_case 5, citation.outgoing 18, citation.incoming 3} and the per-decision channels of every counter row are drawn from exactly those initial channels, with no adversarial-specific channel anywhere in provenance. (f) Only 1 of the 6 counter rows carries counter_evidence_verified=true with a substantive counter_reason; the rest are 'cited in generated answer' with empty or absent evidence, so the labelled statuses are largely not evidence-backed the way MP §6 requires. (g) The human gate is imminent and one-shot: if the map cannot surface a hidden minority line, a jurist's honest verdict is 'no', and the factory would learn that from the single most scarce resource it has. Measuring first costs zero owner attention.

teams.acceptance_test: (1) FREEZE FIRST: commit results/frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability/RULES.json before computing anything — input bundle names with sha256, the frozen legs, every metric definition and every threshold, timestamped earlier than any measured artifact; any later threshold edit must be declared and invalidates the run. (2) A runnable harness that, per bundle and per frozen leg, reports: (a) counter yield — decisions with counter_status in {candidate-limiting, candidate-contrary, contrary_or_exception, limiting} as a share of the bundle; (b) marginal retrieval contribution — how many counter-labelled decisions came from channels NOT present in the initial broad retrieval, computed from per-decision channels/provenance, plus the decision-id set difference between the initial candidate pool and the counter set; (c) rank placement — the distribution of counter rows over the conventional rank order and the share inside the top-10/top-20 that the ranked list already shows; (d) placement visibility — counter rows' cluster_id, is_outlier, and whether they form or join a distinct cluster; (e) evidence quality — share of counter rows with counter_evidence_verified=true and a non-empty counter_reason, and the count whose evidence is the placeholder 'cited in generated answer'; (f) answer linkage — whether the generated answer text actually mentions each counter row's decision_id, per MP §8; (g) language/minority reach — whether any counter row is IT/FR while the consensus cluster is DE-dominant, or older than the bundle median year, i.e. whether the pass reaches minority or language-specific authority at all. (3) Every metric PASS/FAIL or OBSERVED against the frozen thresholds; nothing dropped or reweighted after the fact. (4) At least 3 bundles plus at least 2 of the four frozen reality-check legs re-executed offline from cache; identical inputs -> byte-identical report. (5) NON-VACUITY: the harness must demonstrably FAIL on a corrupted input (counter rows stripped from channels, or ranks randomly permuted), proving the metrics are informative. (6) A single named verdict on the product question — is the counter-authority capability retrieval-independent or classification-only? — with the numbers behind it. (7) IF the verdict is 'classification-only' or the yield fails, exactly ONE bounded candidate cause identified from the evidence already gathered (for example: the adversarial pass receives only the initial bundle and issues no new retrieval variants; or the status gate requires verbatim answer support that minority authority by construction will not have), each with the evidence that points at it and an explicit statement that this team did not test the fix. (8) A short report plus an integration contract stating product owns any change. (9) Zero writes outside frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability/, tests/frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability/, results/frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability/, reports/frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability/ and state/frontier/frontier-adversarial-discoverability.json.
